<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914830_theRebbe_782" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914830_theRebbe_782__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the concept of a "path" as a connecting medium between distant places, using the analogy of a king's road, and applies this to the divine "line" (kav) that connects Ein Sof to the worlds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood based on what is explained in the discourse "Zachor" of the year 5678 (1918)</t>
    <t s="2">by the Baal HaYom HaHuledes (the Rebbe Rashab),</t>
    <t s="3">(on the verse "And they shall guard the way of Havayah"),</t>
    <t s="4">and at length in the Biurei HaZohar of the Mitteler Rebbe</t>
    <t s="5">(on the verse</t>
    <t s="6">"For the ways of Havayah are straight")</t>
    <t s="7">and in many places,</t>
    <t s="8">that the concept of a supernal path is analogous to a physical path</t>
    <t s="9">(in the material sense),</t>
    <t s="10">which is a medium that connects two places that are inherently extremely distant from each other.</t>
    <t s="11">And like the king's road that extends from the capital city, the king's place of residence, to all the far reaches of the country</t>
    <t s="12">(through which one reaches all the large cities),</t>
    <t s="13">and from it branch out further roads and pathways through which one can reach the small towns, etc., until the most remote corner,</t>
    <t s="14">for the distance between the small towns, and certainly the remote corner, and the capital city, the king's place of residence, is not only a spatial distance but also a distance in status,</t>
    <t s="15">to the point of an incomparable distance,</t>
    <t s="16">and through the intermediary of the road, a connection and bond is made between the remote corner and the king's place of residence.</t>
    <t s="17">And this is why the line that extends from Ein Sof is called a "path,"</t>
    <t s="18">for the line is the medium through which [light] is drawn from Ein Sof to the worlds,</t>
    <t s="19">for in addition to the fact that the creation of the worlds</t>
    <t s="20">(the drawing down of Ein Sof light to bring the worlds into existence)</t>
    <t s="21">is through the medium of the line</t>
    <t s="22">[for this matter is through the externality of the line,</t>
    <t s="23">whose source is from Malchus of Ein Sof],</t>
    <t s="24">nevertheless, through the line there is also a drawing down of the revelations of Ein Sof light within the worlds</t>
    <t s="25">[for this matter is through the inwardness of the line,</t>
    <t s="26">whose source is from the hidden Tiferes].</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Torah and mitzvos are called the "way of Havayah" because they draw down the revelation of the essential name Havayah, which is the revelation of the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof, thereby fulfilling the purpose of a dwelling place in the lower realms.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, the Baal HaYom HaHuledes explains in the aforementioned discourse "Zachor"</t>
    <t s="2">that Torah and mitzvos are called the "way of Havayah,"</t>
    <t s="3">for the concept of Torah and mitzvos is to rectify the secret of the Name,</t>
    <t s="4">to draw down the aspect of His great Name</t>
    <t s="5">(the Name Havayah),</t>
    <t s="6">which is the revelation of the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof</t>
    <t s="7">(the aspect of the hidden Tiferes that is above the aspect of Malchus of Ein Sof).</t>
    <t s="8">And therefore it is called the "way of Havayah,"</t>
    <t s="9">the paths through which the revelation of the Name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="10">His great Name, is drawn into the world.</t>
    <t s="11">And through this, the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms is fulfilled,</t>
    <t s="12">the revelation of the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof</t>
    <t s="13">(which is above the aspect of Sovev and Memaleh)</t>
    <t s="14">below in the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="15">in the lowest</t>
    <t s="16">of which there is none lower.</t>
    <t s="17">And he explains there,</t>
    <t s="18">that the concept of a dwelling place in the lower realms is like the analogy of a person dwelling in his friend's house,</t>
    <t s="19">that his entire essence, just as he dwells in his own house, so does he dwell in his friend's house.</t>
    <t s="20">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="21">that the intent of the analogy of a person dwelling in his friend's house</t>
    <t s="22">is to explain,</t>
    <t s="23">that the concept of a dwelling place in the lower realms is not in a manner that, as a result of the revelation of Ein Sof light in the lower being, a refinement and ascent occurs within it</t>
    <t s="24">(in a way that the "lower" aspect is nullified),</t>
    <t s="25">but rather,</t>
    <t s="26">that even after the revelation, it remains a lower being,</t>
    <t s="27">and nevertheless, the revelation of the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof is drawn into it.</t>
    <t s="28">For this is the content of the analogy of a person dwelling in his friend's house,</t>
    <t s="29">that even after he dwells there, the house is still his friend's house,</t>
    <t s="30">and nevertheless, he dwells there with his entire essence just as he dwells in his own house.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the "way of Havayah" serves not only for drawing down from above but also for elevating the lower, achieved through Torah study (drawing down) and the performance of mitzvos with self-compulsion (elevation), as indicated by the verse "and they shall guard the way of Havayah to do charity and justice."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, after this, the discourse continues</t>
    <t s="2">(the aforementioned "Zachor"),</t>
    <t s="3">that just as a physical path serves not only for going but also for returning,</t>
    <t s="4">so too is it with the way of Havayah,</t>
    <t s="5">that its true essence is that it is in a manner that through it, not only is there a drawing down from above to below</t>
    <t s="6">(the concept of going),</t>
    <t s="7">but also an elevation of the lower,</t>
    <t s="8">so that it becomes a vessel for the drawing down.</t>
    <t s="9">And these two matters</t>
    <t s="10">(the drawing down from above and the elevation of the lower)</t>
    <t s="11">are accomplished through the study of Torah and the fulfillment of mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="12">Through the study of Torah, the drawing down of the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof is accomplished</t>
    <t s="13">(for the wisdom of Torah is from the aspect of the wisdom of the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof)</t>
    <t s="14">into the intellect of man</t>
    <t s="15">(human intellect that is clothed in a physical brain),</t>
    <t s="16">and especially when one studies deeply with his intellect, for then it becomes united with him in a wondrous union, the likes of which there is no other,</t>
    <t s="17">to the point that it is called by his name.</t>
    <t s="18">And the refinement and elevation of the lower is accomplished through the performance of mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="19">and especially when the performance of mitzvos is in a manner of "itkafya" (subjugation),</t>
    <t s="20">"maaseh" (action) being a term connoting coercion.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is [the meaning of] "And they shall guard the way of Havayah to do charity and justice,"</t>
    <t s="22">for the true essence of the path that serves not only for going</t>
    <t s="23">(drawing down from above)</t>
    <t s="24">but also for returning</t>
    <t s="25">(refinement and elevation of the lower)</t>
    <t s="26">is that in addition to the study of Torah, there is also the performance of charity,</t>
    <t s="27">for all mitzvos are called by the name "charity."</t>
    <t s="28">And [the verse] adds "charity and justice,"</t>
    <t s="29">that the performance of charity</t>
    <t s="30">(charity in its simple sense)</t>
    <t s="31">must be with justice,</t>
    <t s="32">that one should judge himself regarding his excesses and carefully consider what is absolutely necessary for his soul, and give all the rest to charity.</t>
    <t s="33">And so it is with all the mitzvos</t>
    <t s="34">(which are called by the name "charity,"</t>
    <t s="35">as above)</t>
    <t s="36">that their fulfillment must be in a manner of justice.</t>
    <t s="37">And [the verse] adds "to do"</t>
    <t s="38">(charity and justice),</t>
    <t s="39">that even this</t>
    <t s="40">(that charity is in a manner of justice)</t>
    <t s="41">is still insufficient,</t>
    <t s="42">and it must be in a manner of "itkafya,"</t>
    <t s="43">"maaseh" being a term connoting coercion.</t>
    <t s="44">And through this, the refinement and elevation of the lower is accomplished,</t>
    <t s="45">so that it becomes a vessel for the supernal revelation.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
